BALKAN-TURKISH VAR. THE LAST TRAIN
FRCM TOBACCO, RU TO CONSOLIDATED
CARRYING WOMEN, CHILDREN, REDUCES
AND ABDULLAH PACHA'S STIFF.

Martin H, Donohuo, of the "London Daily Chronicle" describes the departure of this train from Tchorlu and the first few miles of its journey, with women and children packed so closely in the cars that many were crushed and some actually asphyxiated. Owing to the slow pace at which the train was obliged to go to avoid decapitating those who had fallen on the lines, the fugitive soldiers who had sufficient energy cambered on to it. This happened so frequently that soon every inch of space was occupied, even on the front of the engine and the footboards, to which men cluing with the energy born of despair. Others managed to climb on to the roofs, where they hung like so many flies, and some of these were jolled off as the train crossed points or rounded curves and were killed. When the wounded men died during the journey their bodies were lifted out of the train and laid by the roadside, so as to give additional room to the overcrowded living.
BALKAN-TERKISH WAR. THE LAST TRAIN FROM TOPORLU TOCONSTANT MOBILE, CARRING WOMEN, OHLJDREN, REDUGUES AND ABBULLAH PACHA'S STIFF.

Martin H. Donohue, of the "London Daily Chonicle" describes the departure of this train from Tchorlu and the first few miles of its journey, with women and children packed so closely in the cars that many were crushed and some actually asphyxiated. Owing to the slow pace at which the train was obliged to go to avoid recapitating those who had fallen on the lines, the fugitive soldiers who had sufficient energy cambered on to it. This happened so frequently that soon every inch of space was occupied, even on the front of the engine and the footboards, to which men clung with the energy born of despair. Others managed to climb on to the roofs, where they hung like so many flies, and some of these were jolted off as the train crossed points or rounded curves and were killed. When the wounded men died during the journey their bodies were lifted out of the train and laid by the roadside, so as to give additional room to the overcrowded living.
